text:
RETRACTING MY OWN DIAGNOSIS ON THIS BEAD. The cleaner test refutes it. Please do not act on the note I added an hour ago.

WHAT I CLAIMED: that per-call cost scales with the size of the compiled frame, so a full map sweep is quadratic in node count.

THE DECISIVE TEST, which I should have run first. Evaluate THE SAME node (at = 1) while shrinking only the frame around it, holding the domain, the fit, the metric and the support fixed:

  frame nodes    secs/node    vs largest
  320               1.771        1.00x
  160               1.283        0.72x
  40                1.320        0.75x
  10                1.673        0.94x

Going from 320 nodes to 10 - a 32x reduction - changes per-call cost from 1.77 s to 1.67 s, and the trend is non-monotonic: 160 and 40 are both faster than 10. That is noise, not a slope. Per-call cost does NOT depend on frame size.

WHERE MY EARLIER TEST WENT WRONG. In that test I varied the domain from 40 to 320 VOXELS and let node count follow, so P and node count moved together and I attributed the rise to the wrong one. The likely driver is P itself: the metric in these tests is noise_precision(diag(P)), a dense P x P object, so P = 320 carries 64x the elements of P = 40. I built the confound into the design and then read the result as if it were clean.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE NOW SUPPORTS, and it agrees with the exemplar README rather than contradicting it:

  per-node cost is FLAT in the number of nodes evaluated. The README's own figures say so -
  120 nodes in about 22 minutes is 11 s/node, 577 nodes in about 90 minutes is 9.4 s/node.
  Flat, slightly falling.

  so a full sweep is LINEAR in nodes at roughly 9 s each, not quadratic. 577 x 9 s is about
  87 minutes, which is exactly what was observed. There is no super-linear blowup to find.

  and my no-leak result stands - no time or RSS accumulation across 12 sequential calls,
  correlations +0.084 and +0.109, RSS net minus 30 MB.

SO THE REAL QUESTION IS NARROWER AND UNCHANGED FROM THE ORIGINAL FILING: why does ONE node cost ~9 s when rdm() completes all 577 centres in 0.48 s? Not accumulation, not frame size, not condition count - all three now ruled out by measurement. The remaining candidates are the domain feature count P, the support size per sphere (~50 voxels in the exemplar against 6-8 in my tests), and fixed per-call setup that is simply large.

The one experiment I would run next, and did not: hold everything fixed and vary ONLY the support radius, then hold everything fixed and vary ONLY P. Those two are separable and neither of my tests separated them.

PROCESS NOTE. This is the third timing-derived claim of mine to fail verification today, after the 40x crossnobis figure and the auto-is-slowest routes result. It is the worst of the three because the other two were self-inflicted and caught before anyone could act, whereas this one was posted onto someone else's open bead as a diagnosis. The pattern is consistent enough to state as a rule: I should not report a timing-derived cause until I have varied the suspected driver in isolation, holding everything else fixed. Twice today the confound was in my own experimental design rather than in the package.
